Weighted mean and variance (C backend)

Source: R/core_stats.R
cwtd.Rd

The weighted mean and weighted variance of a numeric vector, for data where some observations count for more than others: an average over areas weighted by population, or measurements weighted by how precise each one is. Both come from the compiled core in one pass.

Usage

cwtd(x, w)

Arguments

x

Numeric vector of observations.

w

Numeric vector of non-negative weights, the same length as x. Only their relative sizes matter for the mean; the variance's correction uses them as given.

Value

A named length-2 numeric vector: mean (units of x) and variance (squared units of x).

Details

The mean is \(\bar x_w = \sum_i w_i x_i / \sum_i w_i\). The weights are treated as RELIABILITY weights (how precisely each observation is known), so the variance is $$s_w^2 = \frac{\sum_i w_i (x_i - \bar x_w)^2} {\sum_i w_i - \sum_i w_i^2 / \sum_i w_i},$$ the unbiased estimator under that reading. With every weight equal to 1 it reduces exactly to stats::var(). Frequency weights (a weight of 3 meaning three identical rows) call for the denominator \(\sum w - 1\) instead, and survey design weights call for a design-based variance, so do not use this variance for those.

Refusals: x and w of different lengths ("must have the same length"), any negative weight ("must be non-negative"), and a character, factor or list argument ("must be numeric"). All-zero weights, or an NA in either vector, give NaN for both entries.

See also

cmom() for the unweighted moments, cipw() for inverse-probability weights to feed in here.

Examples

x <- c(10, 20, 30, 40)
w <- c(1, 1, 2, 4)
cwtd(x, w)
#>     mean variance 
#>  31.2500 169.0476 

# The mean agrees with base R.
all.equal(cwtd(x, w)[["mean"]], stats::weighted.mean(x, w))
#> [1] TRUE

# Equal weights recover the unweighted variance.
all.equal(cwtd(x, rep(1, 4))[["variance"]], stats::var(x))
#> [1] TRUE

# A single dominant weight pulls the mean onto that observation.
cwtd(x, c(1, 1, 1, 1000))[["mean"]]
#> [1] 39.94018

# A negative weight is refused.
try(cwtd(x, c(1, -1, 1, 1)))
#> Error : `w` must be non-negative
